Series dependencies multiply failure probabilities ($A_{\text{total}} = A_1 \cdot A_2$), whereas parallel redundant components multiply unavailability ($A_{\text{total}} = 1 - (1 - A_1)(1 - A_2)$).

concept.whyItMatters: Adding a single non-redundant authentication service in the critical path of a 99.99% API immediately caps your system at the weakest link. Understanding Active-Passive vs. Active-Active failover and series/parallel availability math is essential for hitting three-9s (8.77h/yr) or four-9s (52.6m/yr) [SLO error budgets](/concept/slo-sla-error-budgets).
whenToUse: Active-Passive (hot/warm standby) when only one writer/leader can safely hold state or licensing restricts dual-active nodes.
Active-Active when stateless services or multi-region databases can serve traffic simultaneously across zones/regions.
whenNotToUse: Assuming two 99.9% components in sequence give 99.9% availability—in series they drop to 99.8% (doubling downtime).
keyPoints: Active-Passive failover uses heartbeats; if the active node stops responding, the standby promotes (RTO depends on hot vs. cold standby; async replication risks RPO > 0).
Active-Active spreads live traffic across multiple instances via DNS/load balancers—higher utilization and instant blast-radius isolation, but requires conflict resolution for shared writes.
Series formula: $A_{\text{seq}} = \prod_i A_i$; Parallel formula: $A_{\text{par}} = 1 - \prod_i (1 - A_i)$.

sections.content:
## Architecture & Trade-Off Matrix

| Availability | Downtime / Year | Downtime / Month | Downtime / Day | Typical Architecture |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **99% (Two 9s)** | 3.65 days | 7.30 hours | 14.4 min | Single-zone app + scheduled backups |
| **99.9% (Three 9s)** | 8h 45m 57s | 43m 50s | 1m 26s | Multi-AZ app + Active-Passive DB |
| **99.99% (Four 9s)** | 52m 36s | 4m 23s | 8.6s | Auto-failover Multi-AZ + circuit breakers |
| **99.999% (Five 9s)** | 5m 15s | 26.3s | 0.86s | Multi-region Active-Active + zero-downtime deploys |

_recommendedProblem.title: Active-Active Multi-Master Split-Brain Recovery
_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
